This American oceanographer discovered the wrecks of the Titanic, the Bismarck, and the USS Yorktown, and once said finding hydrothermal vents beat finding that famous ocean liner — who is he?
Robert Ballard: Retired US Navy officer and professor of oceanography (born 1942)

From April 7 to July 19, 1994, members of the Tutsi ethnic group, moderate Hutus, and Twa were systematically killed by Hutu militias during a 100-day period in a Central African nation. Over 500,000 to 662,000 people were estimated to have died. What genocide is this?
Rwandan genocide: Mass murder campaign in Rwanda.
Married for more than 40 years to a celebrated general, this English courtier's close bond with Queen Anne made her one of the most powerful women in early 18th-century Britain — who was she?
Sarah Churchill, Duchess of Marlborough: English noblewoman, courtier and politician (1660–1744)
In the Book of Revelation, these divine horn blasts — sounded one at a time by angels after the breaking of the final seal — unleash a series of apocalyptic disasters. What are they called?
Seven trumpets: Described in the Book of Revelation. The seven trumpets are sounded by seven angels and the events that follow are described in detail in Revelation 8–11.
Originating from an Old English word meaning 'being truly guilty,' this concept covers immoral or wrongful thoughts, words, or acts across many religions — what is it?
A onetime Socialist who became a Macron advisor and helped launch En Marche!, this French politician later served briefly as Foreign Minister before joining the European Commission — who is he?
Stéphane Séjourné: French lawyer and politician (born 1985)
This 18th-century French showman and soldier could swallow corks, stones, and live animals, and was constantly ravenous no matter how much he ate — who was he?
Tarrare: French showman and voracious eater (c. 1772–1798)

The third pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, he pushed the empire's borders farther than ever into the Levant and Nubia and is the first king confirmed to have built a tomb in the Valley of the Kings — who was he?
Thutmose I: Third Egyptian Pharaoh of the 18th Dynasty (c. 1506 – 1493 BC)

Political theorist Roger Griffin traced this extreme, supremacist strain of national pride — an ideological foundation beneath Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany — to the view of nations as living organisms with 'great cultural destinies.' What's it called?
A former central bank governor who tamed hyperinflation, he became Ukraine's third president in 2005 on a platform of turning the country toward the EU and NATO. Who is he?
Viktor Yushchenko: President of Ukraine from 2005 to 2010.
Best known for playing 'Trapper' John McIntyre on the CBS series M*A*S*H, this actor later became a regular panelist on a Fox News investing show — who is he?
Hieronymus Karl Friedrich, Freiherr von Münchhausen
Fought between 1939 and 1945, this global conflict remains history's deadliest, claiming 60 to 75 million lives and ending with the only nuclear weapons ever used in war — which conflict?
World War II: 1939–1945 global conflict. World War II, or the Second World War (1 September 1939 – 2 September 1945), was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers.

Regarded as the fourth person to accept Islam, this former slave became the adopted son of the Prophet Muhammad and later commanded early Muslim military expeditions, including a final raid on Byzantine-held Bosra in 629 CE — who was he?
Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi: Companion and adopted son of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four. Qian received his undergraduate education in mechanical engineering at National Chiao Tung University in Shanghai in 1934.
Which one below was established earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin is an astronomer. Despite completing her studies, because she was a woman Payne was not eligible to receive a degree from the University of Cambridge.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium: Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
In what year was Jane Goodall born?
Jane Goodall: Dame Valerie Jane Morris Goodall ( GUUD-awl; née Morris-Goodall; 3 April 1934 – 1 October 2025) was an English primatologist and anthropologist.
In what year was Jan Hus born?
Jan Hus: Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
In what year was Enrico Fermi born?
Enrico Fermi: With his colleagues, Fermi filed several patents related to the use of nuclear power, all of which were taken over by the US government.
In what year did Galileo Galilei die?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year did Paracelsus die?
Paracelsus: Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year was Tardigrade discovered?
Tardigrade: The earliest known fossil is from the Cambrian, some 500 million years ago.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Cannoli: Italy. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Who is credited with discovering Copernicium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Copernicium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
Who is credited with discovering Pluto?
Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Who is credited with discovering Influenza A virus?
Influenza A virus: Christopher Andrewes. Influenza A virus, or IAV, is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
First flown in 1987, this medium-lift helicopter began as a joint UK-Italian venture between Westland and Agusta, and several countries use the nickname 'Merlin' for it — which helicopter is it?
AgustaWestland AW101 is a medium-lift helicopter in military and civil use.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.

Once classified as bacteria and originally called archaebacteria, this domain of mostly single-celled prokaryotic organisms turns out to be the ancestral lineage from which eukaryotes evolved — which domain of life?
Archaea (ar-KEE-) is a domain of organisms.

With the symbol Ba and atomic number 56, this soft, silvery alkaline earth metal is so reactive it's never found free in nature, and takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'heavy' — name this element?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
Formed naturally through evaporation of saline water or generated by salt mining, which concentrated saltwater solution helps de-ice roads and preserve pickled foods?
Brine (or briny water) is a high-concentration solution of salt (typically sodium chloride or calcium chloride) in water.
Chili peppers likely make this hydrophobic compound to deter hungry mammals and fungi — yet it's exactly what gives them their burning, pungent heat. What is it?
Capsaicin (8-methyl-N-vanillyl-6-nonenamide) (commonly) is a toxin that is the main active component of chili peppers and gives them their distinct pungent, "spicy" or "hot" taste.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.
In this satirical action comedy, a group of self-absorbed actors filming a war movie are dropped in the jungle by their fed-up director and must rely on real survival skills. What film is it?
Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
This genus of roughly 340 species includes the carnation and the sweet william, and is nicknamed 'pink' — which genus?

Dianthus (dy-) is a genus of about 340 species of flowering plants in the family Caryophyllaceae, native mainly to Europe and Asia, with a few species in northern and southern Africa, and one species (D. repens) in arctic North America.
Born in Dublin in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family, she's considered the very first woman to work as a medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 - 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.

Native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, this fig species carries deep religious significance across four faiths that originated there, including reverence from Hindu and Jain ascetics — what species is it?
Ficus religiosa is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.

This inflammation of the stomach lining is commonly caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, and can lead to complications like ulcers or, in its autoimmune form, pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis is the inflammation of the lining of the stomach. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.
This medical condition describes a restricted blood supply to tissue or an organ, starving cells of the oxygen they need and often resulting from a blocked or narrowed vessel — what is it called?
Ischemia is a restriction in blood supply to any tissue, muscle group, or organ of the body.

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.
Striking children as they wean, up to about age five, this protein-deficiency disorder produces edema and a fatty, enlarged liver — what is it called?
Kwashiorkor (-kr) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.

This Finnish-American software engineer has led development of a hugely popular open-source operating system kernel since 1991, and also created the distributed version-control system Git — who is he?
Linus Torvalds (born 28 December 1969) is a Finnish and American software engineer who is the creator and lead developer of the Linux kernel since 1991.
This naturally occurring white solid, found as the mineral brucite, has very low water solubility and is a key ingredient in a well-known antacid remedy — what is it?
Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Mg(OH)2.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
Its dust-like, fuzzy, colored appearance on food comes from spores, and its tubular branching network of hyphae counts as a single organism — what fungal structure is it?
Mold (US, PH) or mould (UK, CW) is one of the structures that certain fungi can form.
The paranasal sinuses all drain into this air-filled space that channels inhaled air from the nostrils down toward the throat — what is it?
Nasal cavity is an air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
Belonging to the beech family and encompassing about 500 species across the Northern Hemisphere, this hardwood tree or shrub bears a distinctive nut held in a small cup — name the tree?
Oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
Dubbed the "father of transplantation," this Brazilian-born biologist shared a 1960 Nobel Prize for his discovery of acquired immune tolerance. Who was he?

Peter Medawar (28 February 1915 - 2 October 1987) was a Brazilian-born biologist and writer of Lebanese-British descent who, from a succession of research and teaching posts (Oxford through the Royal Institution), and senior U.K.
Reaching 30 to 50 meters tall and mostly found near rivers and wetlands, this tree genus's hybrid form has proven so tolerant of urban pollution it lines the streets of London — what's the genus?
Platanus is a genus consisting of a small number of tree species.
This sense of self-movement, force, and body position is mediated by receptors located within muscles, tendons, and joints — what is it called?
Proprioception (--) is the sense of self-movement, force, and body position. Proprioception ( PROH-pree-oh-SEP-shən, -⁠ə-) is the sense of self-movement, force, and body position.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).
The first alkali metal denser than water, this element has a radioactive isotope with a half-life more than three times the age of the universe — which element?
Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
Central nervous system depressants in this drug class are often grouped with hypnotics, though technically they're meant to calm rather than induce sleep — what class of drug is this?
Sedative is a substance that induces sedation by reducing irritability or excitement.
This discipline scientifically examines human society, scaling from micro-level individual interactions up to macro-level social systems — what is it?

Sociology is the scientific study of human society that focuses on society, human social behavior, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and aspects of culture associated with everyday life.
This group of cartilaginous fish spans eleven families and roughly 220 species, from tiny river-dwellers to giant manta and devil rays — what group of fish is it?
Stingray are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
Born in 1946, this American serial killer often posed as an authority figure or feigned injury to lure young women to his car before assaulting and murdering them — who was he?
Ted Bundy (n Cowell; November 24, 1946 - January 24, 1989) was an American serial killer who kidnapped, raped and murdered dozens of young women and girls throughout 1974, 1975, and 1978.
This muscular organ in the mouth manipulates food for chewing and swallowing, serves as the body's primary organ of taste, and also enables human speech — what organ is it?
Tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth of a typical tetrapod.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.
A physician and Royal Society charter member, he surveyed confiscated Irish land for Cromwell's soldiers but is best remembered for pioneering 'political arithmetic' in economics — who was he?
William Petty (26 May 1623 - 16 December 1687) was an English economist, physician, scientist and philosopher.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.

Coming on slowly it brings vague fatigue and breathlessness; arriving suddenly it can cause confusion and fainting — and only when it's severe does a person look pale — which blood disorder reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying ability?
Anemia: Reduced ability of blood to carry oxygen.

Named from a Tupi word imitating the sound these macaws make, this genus of large, vividly colored Neotropical parrots includes eight living species prized — and poached — for the pet trade — which genus?
Ara (bird): Neotropical genus of macaws. Ara is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).
Also known as vitamin B7, this B vitamin is found in every living cell and is popularly sold as a supplement; isolated, it's a white needle-like crystal — what is it?
Biotin: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
Certified in Canada in 1998, this large-cabin business jet shares its fuselage cross-section with the Challenger 600 and first flew in 1996 — which jet is it?
Bombardier Global Express: Large cabin business jet. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.

Comprising over 250 species that form small colonies of as few as 50 individuals around a single queen, these fuzzy insects were introduced to New Zealand and Tasmania and can sting repeatedly without dying — which insect is it?
Bumblebee: Genus of insect. A bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.
Designated Alpha Carinae and located some 310 light-years away, this bright giant is the second-brightest star in the night sky, outshone only by Sirius — which star?
Canopus: Brightest star in the constellation of Carina.
A first-generation cephalosporin and β-lactam, this antibiotic can be taken by mouth and treats ear, bone, skin and urinary infections by disrupting bacterial cell-wall growth — what is it?
Cefalexin: Beta-lactam antibiotic. Cefalexin, also spelled cephalexin, is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
Discovered in 1969 and sold under the brand name Lotrimin, this azole-class medication treats athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush — what is it?

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

Governed since 1961 by the Vienna Convention, this practice of using official representatives to influence international relations became a professionalized field in the early 20th century. What is it?
Diplomacy: Practice of conducting negotiations between representatives of groups or states.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.
First synthesized by Paul Janssen in 1960 and sold under brand names like Duragesic, this synthetic opioid runs 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine — what is it?
Fentanyl: Opioid medication. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Madagascar's largest carnivore is a slender, long-tailed mammal that climbs down trees head-first and has convergently evolved so many cat-like features it's been likened to a small cougar — yet it's no cat. What is it?
Fossa (animal): Cat-like, carnivorous mammal endemic to Madagascar.
Running from mouth to anus, this passageway includes the esophagus, stomach, and intestines and handles digestion and nutrient absorption — what is it?
Gastrointestinal tract: Organ system within humans and other animals.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
This Dutch programmer created a popular programming language and held the title 'benevolent dictator for life' until stepping down in 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum: Dutch programmer and creator of Python (born 1956)
Native to Africa south of the Sahara, this domesticated bird has since been introduced everywhere from the West Indies to Australia — which species?
Helmeted guinea fowl: Species of bird. The helmeted guinea fowl (Numida meleagris) is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.
Also called the ratel, this remarkably loose-skinned mammal — able to twist freely inside its own hide — is the largest land member of the weasel family in Africa. What is it?
Honey badger: Species of mammal. The honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel ( or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

Diagnosed via Whipple's triad and most often triggered by diabetes medications like insulin, this condition causes shakiness, confusion, and sweating when blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL — what is it?

Hypoglycemia: Decrease in blood sugar. It is defined as blood glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), symptoms associated with hypoglycemia, and resolution of symptoms when blood sugar returns to normal.
Most often extracted from chicory, this plant-stored fructan earned FDA approval as a dietary fiber in 2018 and remains the gold-standard compound for measuring kidney filtration rates — what is it?
A Communist Party member and Stanford-trained psychiatrist, this woman is best remembered for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer, which put her under FBI surveillance. Who is she?
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Nicknamed the sea devil, frogfish, or fishing frog, this species anchors a major commercial fishery in the Irish Sea and ranges from the Barents Sea to the Mediterranean — which fish?
Lophius piscatorius: Species of fish. Lophius piscatorius, commonly known as the angler, toadfish, sea frog, fishing frog, frogfish, or sea devil, is a species of Lophius in the family Lophiidae.
This category of health conditions arises from too few, too many, or an imbalance of nutrients, and can cause anything from stunted growth to obesity. What is it called?
Malnutrition: Medical condition caused by receiving too little or too many nutrients.

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.

He co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Bill Gates in 1975, then stepped back from daily work in 1983 after a Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis and later launched Vulcan Inc. with his sister. Who was he?
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
